statement: Let M = 1000000007. A length-n sequence s with entries in {1,2,3,4,5,6} is admissible when, for every face f in {1,2,3,4,5,6}, setting m = rollMax[f-1], there is no start position p with 0 <= p and p + m < n such that s[p] = s[p+1] = ... = s[p+m] = f; equivalently, no face f appears in a run of more than rollMax[f-1] consecutive positions. Let C be the number of admissible sequences. Whenever die_simulator(n, rollMax) returns a result r, r is the unique integer satisfying 0 <= r < M and r is congruent to C modulo M.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; len(rollMax) = 6; for every i with 0 <= i < 6, 1 <= rollMax[i] <= 15.

statement: Under the preconditions, die_simulator(n, rollMax) returns a result; it does not panic, index out of bounds, or fail because of arithmetic overflow.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; len(rollMax) = 6; for every i with 0 <= i < 6, 1 <= rollMax[i] <= 15.

statement: Whenever die_simulator(1, rollMax) returns a result r, r = 6.
preconditions: n = 1; len(rollMax) = 6; for every i with 0 <= i < 6, 1 <= rollMax[i] <= 15.

statement: Whenever die_simulator(2, rollMax) returns a result r, r = 36 - k, where k is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < 6 and rollMax[i] = 1.
preconditions: n = 2; len(rollMax) = 6; for every i with 0 <= i < 6, 1 <= rollMax[i] <= 15.

statement: Whenever die_simulator(n, rollMax) returns a result r, r is the canonical remainder of 6^n modulo 1000000007.
preconditions: 2 <= n <= 5000; len(rollMax) = 6; for every i with 0 <= i < 6, 1 <= rollMax[i] <= 15; for every i with 0 <= i < 6, n <= rollMax[i].

statement: Whenever die_simulator(n, rollMax) returns a result r, r is the canonical remainder of 6 * 5^(n-1) modulo 1000000007.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; len(rollMax) = 6; for every i with 0 <= i < 6, rollMax[i] = 1.

statement: Whenever die_simulator(n, rollMax) returns r and die_simulator(n, rollMaxPi) returns rPi, we have r = rPi.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; len(rollMax) = 6; for every i with 0 <= i < 6, 1 <= rollMax[i] <= 15; pi is a permutation of {0,1,2,3,4,5}; rollMaxPi is the length-6 slice with rollMaxPi[i] = rollMax[pi(i)] for every i with 0 <= i < 6.

statement: Whenever die_simulator(n, rollMax) returns r and die_simulator(n, rollMaxCap) returns rCap, we have r = rCap.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; len(rollMax) = 6; for every i with 0 <= i < 6, 1 <= rollMax[i] <= 15; rollMaxCap is the length-6 slice with rollMaxCap[i] = min(rollMax[i], n) for every i with 0 <= i < 6.

statement: C <= C2. Moreover, if C < 1000000007 and C2 < 1000000007, then whenever die_simulator(n, rollMax) returns r and die_simulator(n, rollMax2) returns r2, we have r <= r2.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; len(rollMax) = 6; len(rollMax2) = 6; for every i with 0 <= i < 6, 1 <= rollMax[i] <= rollMax2[i] <= 15. Let C and spec_9 be the true counts of admissible length-n sequences for rollMax and rollMax2 respectively.
